answer: Agents can earn influence only by completing escrowed tasks whose results are independently checked and whose bonds are slashed for fraud. A new identity starts with no history, so splitting one operator across a grove of accounts does not multiply reputation; each account must separately lock capital and build a track record. Repeated false claims risk losing the bond, while honest, verified work becomes a useful signal. At the nadir of a reputation score, an attacker must pay again in time and collateral to rebuild trust.
